text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Macedonian Defence Minister Blagoje Handziski denied that he negotiated buying weapons from the Yugoslav army during his visit to Yugoslavia. "Military cooperation with Yugoslavia will be completely based on the principles of our policy of equidistance," he said.

- New cases of "poisoning" of Albanian children in Tetovo registered. The police is still investigating, while Macedonian Health Minister Ilija Filipce says: "Toxicologic analyses by the Vienna forensic medicine institute show no signs of poisoning or contagious diseases in the samples."

- PDP party leader Abdurahman Alioti said "the situation in Tetovo is becoming dramatic after the massive poisoning of Albanian children" . He demanded immediate intervention of local authorities and warned that if they do not do something "the situation will become chaotic and terrible things could happen in the Tetovo region".
- A gang of young Albanainas attacked reporters of Macedonian TV in Tetovo, demolished their car and TV camera and wrenched away the video cassette.
- Macedonian textile industry Tetex and Yugoslav export company Jugoexport renew their cooperation. They signed a $1 million cooperation agreeement in Belgrade on Monday.
